t: Long ago, two armies faced each other across a valley.
m: Narrator | warm, once-upon-a-time, unhurried | at most 5.2 s
d: Picture: bedtime, you open a big picture book and a child leans on you. (1 Samuel 17:1-3)

t: I am Goliath! Send someone out to fight me!
m: Goliath | booming, bossy, a cartoon giant | at most 4.0 s
d: Picture: you stand in the valley and shout at a whole army, thumping your chest. (1 Samuel 17:8-10)

t: He was almost three metres tall, in bronze armour!
m: Narrator | storyteller, a little amazed, lean on 'three metres' | at most 4.4 s
d: Picture: you stretch your arms up to show how tall he was; the child's eyes go wide. (1 Samuel 17:4-7)

t: He's too big! No one dares!
m: Soldiers | scared, quick, several people at once | at most 2.6 s
d: Picture: a few soldiers peeking out from behind their shields. (1 Samuel 17:11, 24)

t: Ha ha! You're all too scared!
m: Goliath | smug laugh, mocking | at most 3.0 s
d: Picture: nobody comes out; you throw your head back and laugh, banging your spear. (1 Samuel 17:10, 16)

t: Then David came, a young shepherd boy. He was not afraid.
m: Narrator | a turn in the story, light, firm at the end | at most 5.0 s
d: Picture: a boy with a lunch basket walks in from far away; you point him out with a smile. (1 Samuel 17:20-23)

t: Don't be afraid! I'll fight him!
m: David | brave, clear, not shouting | at most 2.8 s
d: Picture: you step in front of everyone, stand tall, and say it plainly. (1 Samuel 17:32)

t: You're just a boy. How can you win?
m: Saul | kind but worried, like a grandpa | at most 3.4 s
d: Picture: the king bends down, a hand on the boy's shoulder, frowning. (1 Samuel 17:33)

t: I kept sheep. I beat a lion and a bear!
m: David | confident, telling his own story | at most 4.3 s
d: Picture: you act out the lion and the bear as you speak. (1 Samuel 17:34-36)

t: The LORD saved me then. He'll save me now!
m: David | quiet faith, sincere | at most 3.9 s
d: Picture: you look up at the sky and say it softly but surely. (1 Samuel 17:37)

t: Too heavy! I'll go without this armour.
m: David | a bit funny, the armour is far too big | at most 3.3 s
d: Picture: you clank two steps in armour three sizes too big and nearly fall over. (1 Samuel 17:38-39)

t: By the brook, David picked five smooth stones.
m: Narrator | soft and careful, like counting stones | at most 4.0 s
d: Picture: a bubbling brook; you pick up the stones one by one. (1 Samuel 17:40)

t: Little boy, you want to fight me?
m: Goliath | scornful, teasing | at most 3.2 s
d: Picture: you bend down to look at the little boy and laugh at him. (1 Samuel 17:42-44)

t: You come with sword and spear. I come in the name of the LORD!
m: David | the key line: firm, ringing, not angry | at most 6.0 s
d: Picture: the giant is right in front of you; you don't step back and your voice fills the valley. (1 Samuel 17:45)

t: David ran forward and swung his sling!
m: Narrator | tense, faster, a little hushed | at most 3.0 s
d: Picture: holding your breath as the boy runs and the sling whirls. (1 Samuel 17:48-49)

t: The stone hit his forehead. Down fell the giant!
m: Narrator | quick, then slow and heavy on 'Down' | at most 3.9 s
d: Picture: the stone flies -- thump! you slap the book; the child jumps, then laughs. (1 Samuel 17:49-50)

t: The battle belongs to the LORD!
m: David | joyful, thankful, not boasting | at most 2.6 s
d: Picture: everyone cheers; you raise your hands and give the glory to God. (1 Samuel 17:47)

t: Courage and trust in God matter more than size!
m: Narrator | bright, warm ending, to the child | at most 4.3 s
d: Picture: the story is over; you close the book and pat the child's head. (1 Samuel 17:45-47 (moral))
